name: model-connectivity
title: Model Connectivity Network — How the Curated Models Couple
question:
Do the curated BioModels/Physiome/PhysioNet models form a connected network
through shared biological variables — shared molecular species and shared HRA
anatomy — and is there a dominant mechanistic backbone, or just isolated
islands?

study_card.goal: Build a model-to-model connectivity network over the curated corpus DB: edges for shared molecular species (CHEBI/UniProt/KEGG/GO/Reactome) and shared HRA anatomy (organ/FTU/cell-type), and materialize it as an interactive force-graph explorer.
study_card.mechanism: ModelConnectivityNetwork.update -> build_network(model_hra_map.json): per-model variable tokens -> drop ubiquitous stop-words (>15% document-frequency) -> inverted index -> pairwise shared-variable counts -> per-node strongest edges (two layers) -> union-find components -> network.json + the self-contained force-graph viewer under viz/network/.
study_card.expected_result: A non-empty node set with a dominant connected component on the molecular layer, hub variables that are core biology (ATP, translation), and a parallel anatomy layer — all navigable in the Model Connectivity Network explorer.
study_card.main_expert_question: A shared identifier means two models reference the same species; which of the densest edges are actually mechanistically composable (compatible units / rate laws)?

biological_summary:
Mechanistic models are authored in isolation but describe one coupled
biology. This study makes the latent connectivity of the curated corpus
explicit: it reads each model's own curated molecular-species identifiers and
anatomical annotations from the biomodel->HRA map DB and links two models
wherever they share them. Ubiquitous "stop-word" variables (e.g. GO:0005623
"cell") are dropped so generic terms do not create a meaningless hairball, and
each model keeps only its strongest edges. The resulting network's shape is
the finding: a dense mechanistic backbone of energy-metabolism and
gene-expression machinery that most models touch, with tissue-specific models
hanging off it — the integration map that shows where existing models already
overlap and could be composed.
readouts: stats.n_nodes / n_models_total (connected node set vs full corpus)

report.title: Model Connectivity Network — 1,456 models link into a 634-model mechanistic backbone
report.objective:
Do the curated models connect through shared biological variables, and is
there a dominant mechanistic backbone?
report.conclusion:
Over the 2,554-model curated corpus, 1,456 models carry at least one
shareable variable. The molecular layer (stop-word variables above 15%
document-frequency dropped, each node kept to its strongest edges) links
them with 3,469 edges into 754 components whose largest spans 634 models
(43.5% of the connected set) — a single dominant mechanistic backbone, not
isolated islands. Its hub variables are core biology: ATP (CHEBI:15422, 83
models), translation (GO:0006412, 119), protein catabolism (GO:0030163,
104), apoptosis (GO:0008219, 101). A parallel anatomy layer adds 1,704
tissue co-location edges (organ-tagged 873 models, FTU 631, cell-type 580).
The whole network is navigable in the new Model Connectivity Network
explorer.
report.caveat:
An edge is identifier CO-OCCURRENCE, not verified mechanistic
compatibility: a shared CHEBI/UniProt id means both models reference that
species, not that their rate laws, units, or assumptions agree. The graph is
pruned for legibility (stop-word variables dropped, strongest edges kept),
and 1,098/2,554 models (43%) carry no shareable variable in the current
annotations and are absent.

findings.statement:
The curated corpus is a connected shared-variable system, not a scatter of
isolated models: 1,456 models link through shared molecular species into a
dominant 634-model component (43.5%) centered on core-metabolism hub
variables (ATP, translation, apoptosis), with a parallel 1,704-edge anatomy
layer. This is an emergent property of independent curation practice — the
same species and tissues recur across models authored in isolation — and it
gives a concrete integration map of where existing models already overlap.

evidence.summary: 1,456/2,554 models connected; molecular layer 3,469 edges, 754 components, largest 634 (43.5%); hubs ATP (83), translation (119), apoptosis (101); anatomy layer 1,704 edges (organs 873 / FTU 631 / cell-types 580); molecular coverage GO 967 / UniProt 507 / CHEBI 480 / KEGG 322 / HGNC 302 / Reactome 105 / Ensembl 360.

regression_compatibility.basis: The ModelConnectivityNetwork step builds deterministically (identical edge set across runs) and materializes a non-empty two-layer network + the viewer pack without error.

biological_validation.basis: The connected-backbone finding is directly measured from the corpus annotations and is real; but edges are identifier co-occurrence, not verified mechanistic compatibility, so the network marks candidate couplings a modeler must still validate.

explanatory_gain.basis: F-01 reframes the corpus from a flat catalog into a navigable coupling network with an identifiable core, turning 'how do our models connect?' into an explorable map — the investigation's central integrative claim.

limitations: Edges are identifier co-occurrence, not verified mechanistic compatibility (shared species, not agreed rate laws/units) — the network marks candidate couplings, not confirmed compositions.

The graph is pruned for legibility: variables above 15% document-frequency are dropped and each node keeps only its strongest edges, so it shows the strongest couplings rather than every shared variable.
1,098/2,554 models (43%) carry no shareable variable in the current annotations and are absent from the network; richer annotation would connect more.

resolved_uncertainties: The curated corpus is connected, not isolated: a single molecular backbone spans 43.5% of the connected set, centered on core-metabolism variables.
remaining_uncertainties: Which of the densest co-occurrence edges are actually mechanistically composable (compatible units/rate laws)?
Would richer molecular/anatomical annotation connect the 1,098 currently-unshareable models?

followup_study_proposals.title: Validate the strongest edges as real compositions
followup_study_proposals.motivation: A shared-identifier edge is a candidate coupling; the natural next step is to test whether the densest edges can be wired into a working process-bigraph composition (compatible units/rate laws), turning candidate couplings into verified ones.
followup_study_proposals.proposed_experiment: Take the top-weight molecular edges in the backbone (e.g. models sharing ATP + a pathway) and attempt a two-model process-bigraph composition through the shared species, recording which compose cleanly vs need unit/rate-law reconciliation.

alternative_hypotheses.claim: The network's connectivity might be an artifact of ubiquitous generic terms (e.g. "cell", "cytoplasm") rather than meaningful shared biology.
alternative_hypotheses.discriminated_by: those stop-word variables (document-frequency above 15% of nodes) are dropped before edges are drawn, and the corpus still forms a dominant 634-model (43.5%) component around specific hub variables like ATP and translation — so the backbone is genuine shared mechanism, not a generic-term hairball.

alternative_hypotheses.claim: A shared identifier might only reflect shared annotation practice, not biology two models could actually couple through.
alternative_hypotheses.discriminated_by: not resolved here; whether a co-occurrence edge is a real mechanistic coupling (compatible units/rate laws) is the study's open expert question (fp-compose-strongest-edges).
